mots.sens: This term means 'house of the Lord'. It evokes not only a physical place but also the presence of God among His people. The house of the Lord is a symbol of communion between God and Israel, highlighting the importance of holiness and devotion in worship. Spiritually, it reminds believers that their lives should be a sanctuary for the divine presence.

This word designates an altar, a place of sacrifice and offering. In Israelite culture, the altar is the meeting point between man and God, where expiatory sacrifices are offered for the forgiveness of sins. Theologically, this underscores the need for reconciliation with God and the importance of sacrifice, foreshadowing Christ's ultimate sacrifice for humanity.

This term means 'burnt offering', a type of sacrifice that is completely consumed in honor of God. The burnt offering symbolizes total devotion and surrender to God, representing a self-offering. In a spiritual context, it reminds us of the call to give ourselves entirely to God, acknowledging His sovereignty and grace.

1.epoque: This passage is set in the time of David, king of Israel, towards the end of his reign, as he prepares for the construction of the temple of the Lord.
1.passage: In this chapter, David expresses his desire to build a house for God, but he receives the instruction that it will be his son Solomon who will accomplish this task. This highlights the importance of the house of God in Israelite worship.
1.culture: In Israelite culture, the construction of a temple was a central act of devotion and recognition of God's sovereignty. Altars were sacred places where the people gathered to worship and offer sacrifices.
1.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the house of God as a place of encounter with the divine. It also reminds us that worship must be centered on devotion and authentic adoration, symbolized by the altar of burnt offerings.
1.commentaire: David, by declaring that this place will be the house of the Lord, teaches us the importance of dedicating our lives and spaces to God. As believers, we are called to make our hearts a sanctuary for God, offering our lives as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to Him. This verse reminds us that our worship must be authentic and centered on God's will.

mots.sens: This word means 'stone' and designates a fundamental element in construction. In the context of the temple's construction, it evokes not only solidity and durability but also the idea of spiritual foundation. Theologically, stones can symbolize believers, who are 'built up' together to form a spiritual temple.

This term designates 'weight' or 'measure', often associated with the idea of preparation and value. In this verse, it underscores the importance of meticulous preparation for the work of God. Spiritually, it reminds us that our service to the Lord must be done with care and seriousness.

This word means 'house' and is often used to refer to the temple of God. In the biblical context, the house of God represents the divine presence among His people. This highlights the importance of the community of believers and the need for a sanctuary to worship and serve God.

This term designates a 'foreigner' or 'resident' and refers to non-Israelites living in Israel. This shows the inclusivity of God's people, where even those who are not of Israelite descent can participate in the divine work. Theologically, this foreshadows the opening of the Gospel to the nations.

2.epoque: This passage is set in the time of David, king of Israel, around the 10th century B.C., a period marked by the unification of the Israelite tribes and the establishment of Jerusalem as the religious and political capital.
2.passage: In this chapter, David prepares for the construction of the temple of God, a project he will not be able to accomplish himself due to war. He ensures that the necessary resources are gathered so that his son Solomon can fulfill this sacred task.
2.culture: In ancient culture, the construction of temples was an act of devotion and consecration. The materials used, such as hewn stones, were carefully selected to honor the deity and reflect God's greatness.
2.interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of preparation and collaboration in the work of God. David gathers not only resources but also people, showing that everyone has a role to play in building the kingdom of God.
2.commentaire: This passage teaches us that the construction of the house of God requires both material resources and an engaged community. As believers, we are called to contribute to God's work, each with our gifts and talents. It also reminds us that the Church is a place of welcome, where all, including those considered foreigners, can participate in the glory of God.

mots.sens: This word means 'iron' and evokes solidity and resilience. In the biblical context, iron is often associated with strength and durability, symbolizing protection and security. Spiritually, it can represent the strength that God gives His people to build and defend their faith.

This term designates 'bronze' or 'copper', a precious metal used for various valuable objects. In the Bible, bronze is often linked to purification and redemption, as a symbol of what is precious in God's eyes. Here, its mention underscores the importance of quality materials for the construction of the temple.

This word means 'gates', representing not only physical entrances but also spiritual accesses. Gates are symbols of protection, security, and welcome. In the context of the temple, they symbolize access to the presence of God and the importance of a worthy entrance into the holy place.

3.epoque: This passage is set in the time of David, just before the construction of Solomon's temple, a period of preparation and planning for worship of the God of Israel.
3.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David prepares to build the temple, but leaves this task to his son Solomon. This verse highlights David's efforts to gather the necessary materials for this sacred work.
3.culture: In ancient culture, the construction of temples was an act of devotion and grandeur. The materials used were carefully chosen to reflect God's glory and the importance of the place of worship.
3.interpretation: This verse reminds us of the importance of preparing our hearts and our environment to welcome the presence of God. The quality materials used for the temple also symbolize our commitment to offer the best to God in our service and worship.
3.commentaire: David's preparation for the construction of the temple teaches us the importance of diligence and foresight in our spiritual lives. By committing to offer the best to God, we honor His presence and prepare our lives to be places of encounter with Him. May we be inspired to build our faith with quality spiritual materials.

mots.sens: The word 'erez' refers to the cedar, a majestic and durable tree, often associated with strength and longevity. In the biblical context, it symbolizes nobility and prosperity, being used for the construction of temples and palaces. Spiritually, the cedar represents the solidity of faith and the presence of God, which is often compared to a tree planted by the waters.

The word 'tsor' refers to the region of Tyre, famous for its artisans and maritime trade. The Tyrians were renowned for their skill in woodworking, particularly with cedar, which was highly prized in architecture. Spiritually, this underscores the importance of collaboration between nations for God's work, showing that even external sources can contribute to God's glory.

4.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of David, towards the end of his life, when his son Solomon is preparing to build the temple in Jerusalem, a monumental project that requires considerable resources.
4.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David prepares for the construction of the temple, an act of devotion to God. This verse highlights divine provision through the Sidonians and Tyrians, who bring essential materials.
4.culture: The culture of the time valued trade and alliances between nations, and the cedar was a symbol of wealth and prestige. The materials imported from other regions testify to the interconnectedness of different peoples.
4.interpretation: This verse illustrates how God provides for the needs of His people through unexpected means, even through foreign nations. It reminds us that generosity and collaboration can be instruments of divine will.
4.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of recognizing and appreciating the resources that God provides, even through those we consider outside our community. As believers, we should be open to how God acts in our lives and use the gifts and resources He sends us to build His kingdom.

mots.sens: This word means 'son' and is often used in the Bible to denote not only a biological relationship but also a spiritual one. In this context, it emphasizes David's responsibility towards Solomon, his son, as the future king and builder of the temple. It also evokes the notion of succession and the spiritual heritage passed down from generation to generation.

The term 'house' refers not only to a physical structure but also to a place of meeting with God. In the context of the temple's construction, it symbolizes the place where the divine presence resides among His people. This word underscores the importance of holiness and devotion in the establishment of a place of worship.

This word means 'glory' and refers to the magnificence and majesty of God. In this verse, it evokes the impact that the temple will have on the nations, reflecting God's greatness through Solomon's work. It also emphasizes the importance of giving God glory in all our endeavors.

This verb means 'to prepare' or 'to equip' and implies an act of planning and devotion. By preparing for the construction of the temple, David shows his commitment to honor God and establish a place of worship. This reminds us of the importance of being spiritually and materially prepared for the works that God calls us to accomplish.

5.epoque: This passage takes place at the end of David's reign, as he prepares to pass the kingdom to his son Solomon, marking an important transition in the history of Israel.
5.passage: In this chapter, David focuses on preparing for the construction of the temple, a project he had in his heart but could not accomplish himself. This shows his desire to see a place of worship established for the Lord.
5.culture: In Israelite culture, the construction of a temple was an act of supreme devotion, symbolizing God's presence among His people. Kings were often judged by their ability to establish and maintain places of worship.
5.interpretation: This verse illustrates David's responsibility as a father and king, emphasizing the importance of preparing the next generation to serve God. It also reminds us that even though Solomon is young, God has a plan for him and for the temple he will build.
5.commentaire: David, by preparing the way for Solomon, teaches us the importance of preparing future generations in faith. We are called to invest in the spiritual lives of those around us, equipping them for the works that God has planned for them. This passage encourages us to be builders of faith, committing to honor God in all that we undertake.

mots.sens: The word 'bayit' means 'house' or 'home'. In this context, it is not limited to a physical structure but also evokes the idea of God's presence among His people. The house that Solomon is to build is intended to be a place of meeting between God and Israel, thus highlighting the importance of holiness and worship in communal life.

The term 'tsivah' means 'to command' or 'to order'. This implies authority and responsibility, emphasizing that David, as king, acts under divine inspiration. This word highlights the importance of obedience to God's will, particularly in spiritual and communal matters.

The word 'El' refers to God in His supreme power. In this verse, it reminds us that the house to be built is not simply a building, but a place dedicated to the God of Israel, who is the creator and sovereign. This underscores the centrality of God in the life of Israel and the importance of recognizing Him in all endeavors.

The word 'Shalom' means 'peace' and 'completeness'. It is often associated with Solomon, whose name is derived from this term. In the context of the temple's construction, it evokes the idea that peace and harmony are essential to God's presence among His people, and that the house must reflect this divine peace.

6.epoque: This verse takes place at the end of David's reign, as he prepares for the transition to the reign of his son Solomon, marking a crucial moment in the history of Israel.
6.passage: In this chapter, David prepares for the construction of the temple, a project he had in his heart but could not accomplish himself. He passes this task to Solomon, emphasizing the importance of this project for the people of Israel.
6.culture: At this time, the construction of temples for gods was a common practice in the ancient world. However, the temple of Israel stands out for its unique character, being dedicated to the living God, in contrast to the idols of surrounding nations.
6.interpretation: This passage illustrates the responsibility of each generation to pass on faith and God's projects. By commanding Solomon to build the temple, David shows that constructing a place of worship is essential for the relationship between God and His people.
6.commentaire: This verse reminds us of the importance of obedience to God's call in our lives. Just as David prepared his son to accomplish a work for the Lord, we are called to encourage and equip future generations to serve God. Building a 'house' for God, whether in our hearts or in our communities, is an act of devotion and faith.

mots.sens: This word means 'house' and refers not only to a physical building but also to a home, a place of refuge and safety. In the biblical context, it often symbolizes the presence of God among His people. The construction of a house for the Lord represents the desire to establish a sacred place where the community can worship and meet God.

This term is a relative pronoun meaning 'who,' 'that,' or 'in which.' It introduces a relationship or condition, linking the act of building to the object of that action, here the house of the Lord. Spiritually, this underscores the importance of divine will in human projects, indicating that any endeavor for God must align with His will.

This word means 'heart' and refers to the inner part of a person, the seat of emotions, thoughts, and decisions. In the Bible, the heart is often associated with spiritual commitment and devotion to God. David's intention to build a house for the Lord reveals his deep desire to serve God with all his being.

7.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of David, towards the end of his life, as his son Solomon is about to succeed him. It is a pivotal time for the people of Israel, marked by the consolidation of the kingdom and the desire to build a temple for God.
7.passage: In this chapter, David prepares for the construction of the temple by gathering materials and instructing Solomon. This verse highlights David's intention to build a house for the Lord, showing the importance of this project in the spiritual life of Israel.
7.culture: In Israelite culture, the construction of a temple was an act of devotion and recognition of God's sovereignty. The temple represented God's presence among His people and was central to religious and communal life.
7.interpretation: David's intention to build a house for the Lord reveals his heart for God and his desire to honor Him. This teaches us that our projects should be motivated by a desire to glorify God and align with His purposes.
7.commentaire: This verse reminds us of the importance of our intentions and projects for God. Like David, we should seek to honor God in all that we undertake, ensuring that our actions align with His will. May our desire to serve God always be at the center of our hearts and lives.

mots.sens: This word means 'blood' and evokes life, death, and sacrifice. In the biblical context, blood is often associated with guilt and judgment, but also with redemption. Here, it emphasizes the gravity of David's actions, who, despite his heart for God, committed acts of violence that disqualified him from building the temple.

This term means 'house' and can refer to both a dwelling and the temple of God. In the Bible, the house of God is a symbol of His presence among His people. The fact that David cannot build this house underscores the importance of purity and holiness in serving God.

This word means 'war' or 'combat' and refers to conflicts and struggles. In the Scriptures, wars are often interpreted as struggles between good and evil, and here they remind us of the consequences of human actions on divine will. This highlights the need for peace and reconciliation in God's plan.

This word means 'word' or 'thing' and is often used to refer to the word of God. In this context, it emphasizes divine authority and the clear communication of God's will to David. It reminds us that God's guidance is essential for the fulfillment of His promises.

8.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of David, around the 10th century B.C., a period marked by the unification of the tribes of Israel and military conquests.
8.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David prepares for the construction of the temple and conveys his instructions to Solomon. This verse highlights the reason why David cannot carry out this project, despite his ardent desire.
8.culture: The culture of the time valued war and military courage, but also holiness and purity in worship. The construction of the temple was an act of supreme devotion, requiring spiritual preparation.
8.interpretation: This verse highlights God's justice and the necessity of purity in service. David, though a man after God's own heart, is reminded of the reality of the consequences of his actions. This teaches us that our commitment to God must be accompanied by a life that conforms to His expectations.
8.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God looks at the heart and life of His servants. Even if we have great intentions, our past and actions have consequences. This encourages us to seek reconciliation and purification in our relationship with God, so that we can fully serve in His plans.

mots.sens: The word 'shalom' means peace, wholeness, and well-being. It is derived from the root 'šlm' which evokes the idea of completeness and security. In this verse, it underscores God's divine promise of peace and tranquility for Israel under Solomon's reign, which has significant theological implications, as it illustrates God's desire to restore and maintain harmony among His people.

The term 'manoaḥ' means rest or tranquility. It is often used to describe a state of calm and security, particularly in relation to deliverance from enemies. In the context of this verse, it evokes not only physical rest but also spiritual rest, indicating that Solomon will bring an era of peace that will allow the people to focus on their relationship with God.

The word 'oyev' means enemy. It comes from the root 'איב' which means to be hostile or in opposition. In this verse, the mention of enemies highlights the challenges Israel faced, but also God's promise of protection and deliverance, thereby reinforcing the people's trust in divine faithfulness.

9.epoque: This verse is set in the context of the Old Testament, during a time when Israel was a unified kingdom under David's leadership, and where divine promises were crucial for the national and spiritual identity of the people.
9.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David prepares for the construction of the temple and conveys instructions to Solomon, his son. This passage emphasizes the importance of the peace and rest that Solomon will bring, contrasting with the struggles and wars of previous generations.
9.culture: In Israelite culture, peace and security were signs of divine blessing. Solomon's reign is often seen as a golden age, where prosperity and tranquility were tangible realities for the people.
9.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse foreshadows Christ, who is the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6). Just as Solomon, Jesus brings true rest and lasting peace to those who believe in Him, delivering them from their spiritual enemies.
9.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is a God of promise and peace. As believers, we can rest in the assurance that, even amidst struggles, God offers us rest in Christ. We are called to live in this peace, share it with those around us, and remember that our true security is found in Him.

mots.sens: This word means 'son' and is used to denote a direct familial relationship. In this context, it emphasizes the intimate relationship between God and Solomon, where God presents Himself as a protective and loving father. It also establishes a promise of continuity and legitimacy for Solomon's reign, who is seen as the chosen heir of God.

This term translates to 'house' or 'sanctuary' and refers to the place of God's residence among His people. In this verse, it evokes the idea of a sacred space where God dwells and where His name is glorified. The construction of this house is an act of devotion, symbolizing the divine presence and the people's commitment to God.

This word means 'kingdom' and refers to authority and sovereignty. In the context of this verse, it highlights the establishment of Solomon's throne as a divine institution, ensuring the stability and longevity of Israel's reign. This underscores God's plan for His people and the promise of His protection.

10.epoque: This passage is set during the time of David, king of Israel, just before the transition of power to his son Solomon. It is a pivotal period where the foundations of the kingdom of Israel are being established and the construction of the temple is being contemplated.
10.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David prepares for the construction of the temple and gives his instructions to Solomon. This chapter highlights God's desire to dwell among His people through the construction of this house dedicated to His name.
10.culture: In Israelite culture, the construction of a temple was an act of great spiritual and national significance. It represented not only a place of worship but also a symbol of the identity and unity of the people under God's sovereignty.
10.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise made to Solomon, who is both an heir and a servant of God. The father-son relationship between God and Solomon illustrates God's closeness to His people and His commitment to establishing a just and enduring kingdom.
10.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God desires to establish a personal relationship with each of us, just as He did with Solomon. By building our lives on the foundations of His word and dedicating our actions to Him, we participate in the building of His kingdom on earth. Let us be encouraged to seek His presence and to build sanctuaries in our hearts, where He can dwell and reign.

mots.sens: This term designates God, the Almighty. It evokes strength, power, and divine authority. In the biblical context, 'El' underscores the relationship between God and His people, indicating that it is through His presence and support that one can accomplish works worthy of Him. Spiritually, this reminds believers that all success comes from the Lord.

This verb means 'to build' or 'to construct.' It implies not only the physical act of building but also the idea of founding something lasting and significant. In the context of the temple's construction, it represents the establishment of a meeting place between God and His people, highlighting the importance of the divine presence in the lives of believers.

This word means 'peace,' but it also encompasses notions of prosperity, well-being, and harmony. In the context of this verse, the peace of the Lord is essential for the success of the construction project. Theologically, this reminds us that true prosperity is linked to the presence and blessing of God in our lives.

11.epoque: This verse is set during the time of the Israelite monarchy, under the reign of David, as his son Solomon is being prepared to become king and to build the temple of the Lord.
11.passage: In this chapter, David speaks to his son Solomon, entrusting him with the task of building the temple. This moment is crucial as it marks the transition of royalty and the importance of God's house in the life of Israel.
11.culture: In Israelite culture, the construction of a temple was a sacred and symbolic act, representing the presence of God among His people. The temple was the center of religious and social life, and its construction was seen as a divine mission.
11.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of God's presence in any project we undertake. Prosperity and success can only come from the Lord, and it is essential to recognize His sovereignty and support in our efforts.
11.commentaire: As believers, we are called to build our lives on solid foundations, relying on the presence and promises of God. This verse reminds us that everything we undertake should be done in communion with Him, so that we may prosper according to His will. May our prayer be that the Lord is with us in every project, so that we may glorify His name.

mots.sens: This term means 'wisdom' and denotes a deep and practical understanding of things. It evokes not only intellectual knowledge but also the ability to apply it in daily life. In the context of governance, wisdom is essential for making just decisions in accordance with God's will.

The word 'understanding' refers to the ability to discern and comprehend complex situations. It implies an aptitude for grasping the nuances of events and acting with discernment. Spiritually, understanding is a gift that God grants to guide His people in truth and justice.

The term 'to reign' denotes the action of governing or exercising authority. In the Bible, reign is often associated with the responsibility to lead according to divine precepts. This underscores the importance of spiritual leadership aligned with God's law, essential for the well-being of the nation.

The word 'law' refers to the entirety of the commandments and instructions given by God. It represents the moral and ethical foundation upon which a government must rely. God's law is a guide for living in harmony with Him and with others, and it is crucial for the success of the reign.

12.epoque: This passage is set during the time of the Israelite monarchy, when David prepares for the succession of his son Solomon as king of Israel.
12.passage: In this chapter, David charges Solomon with building the temple and conveys to him the importance of wisdom and obedience to God's law for successful reign.
12.culture: At this time, wisdom was highly valued in Israelite culture, often associated with the ability to govern and understand God's ways.
12.interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true wisdom and understanding come from God and are essential for effective leadership. It reminds us that a king's success depends on his commitment to following divine law.
12.commentaire: This passage teaches us that spiritual and moral leadership relies on the pursuit of divine wisdom. As believers, we should also pray for wisdom and understanding in our daily lives, so that we may live according to God's precepts and positively influence those around us.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to be strong', 'to take courage', or 'to strengthen oneself'. It evokes the idea of solidity and determination in the face of challenges. In this context, it emphasizes the importance of inner strength to fulfill God's will, especially in times of uncertainty or fear. Spiritually, it reminds us that our strength comes from our faith in God.

This term refers to the 'law' or 'teaching' of God, often associated with the instructions given to Moses. It implies not only commandments but also guidance for living according to divine will. In this verse, observance of the Torah is presented as essential for prosperity, highlighting the importance of living in accordance with divine principles in our daily lives.

This word means 'God' and is used to denote divine power and God's sovereignty over all creation. In the context of this verse, it reminds us that it is the Lord who gives laws and ordinances, and that He is the source of all strength and prosperity. Spiritually, it invites us to recognize God's authority in our lives and to submit to His will.

13.epoque: This passage is set during the time of the Israelite monarchy, when David is preparing his son Solomon to build the temple. It is a period of transition and spiritual preparation for Israel.
13.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David speaks to Solomon, giving him valuable instructions regarding the construction of the temple. This chapter emphasizes the importance of faithfulness to God's law and Solomon's role as a spiritual leader.
13.culture: The Israelite culture valued obedience to divine laws as the foundation of national and personal prosperity. The construction of the temple was a central act of devotion and recognition of God's sovereignty.
13.interpretation: This verse teaches that prosperity and spiritual strength depend on obedience to God's commandments. It encourages us not to yield to fear but to strengthen ourselves in faith, relying on divine promises.
13.commentaire: This passage reminds us that our success in spiritual and material life is linked to our commitment to follow God's instructions. As believers, we must strengthen ourselves in our faith and act with courage, knowing that God is with us. Let us put His word into practice to experience His blessing and prosperity in all aspects of our lives.

mots.sens: The word 'bayit' refers to a house, but in the biblical context, it often refers to the house of God, a place of meeting between heaven and earth. This term evokes not only a physical building but also a spiritual reality where the divine presence dwells. In this verse, it highlights the importance of the house of the Lord as a center of worship and communion with God.

The word 'kesef' means silver, but it is also used to denote value and price. In biblical culture, money is often associated with material wealth, but also with the idea of redemption and sacrifice. In this verse, it underscores the importance of material resources dedicated to the construction of the temple, symbolizing an act of devotion to God.

The word 'oz' means strength or power. It evokes solidity and durability, often in relation to divine strength. In this context, it alludes to the robustness of materials like iron and bronze, which are essential for building a house worthy of the Lord, thus reflecting God's greatness and the solidity of His work.

The verb 'hekin' means to prepare or establish. It implies a deliberate effort and intention to set up something significant. In this verse, it highlights David's commitment to prepare the necessary resources for the house of the Lord, illustrating the importance of spiritual and material preparation in our service to God.

14.epoque: This verse is set during the reign of David, before the construction of the temple, when David is preparing to pass the project to his son Solomon.
14.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David speaks of his efforts to prepare for the construction of the temple, a project that was dear to him. This chapter emphasizes the importance of the house of God and the responsibility of each generation to contribute to its building.
14.culture: In Israelite culture, the construction of a temple was an act of supreme devotion, representing God's presence among His people. Material resources were seen as sacred offerings intended to honor the Lord.
14.interpretation: This verse reminds us that preparation for the service of God requires effort and resources. It also emphasizes the importance of giving generously for God's cause, recognizing that all we have comes from Him.
14.commentaire: David's commitment to prepare the materials for the temple teaches us the importance of diligence and preparation in our spiritual lives. As believers, we are called to invest our resources, both material and spiritual, for the work of God. This invites us to reflect on how we can contribute to the building of the Church and the glory of God in our community.

mots.sens: This term designates a 'worker' or 'servant', and it evokes the idea of diligent and devoted work. It is often used to describe those engaged in a specific task, particularly in the context of serving God. In this verse, it underscores the importance of labor in the construction of the temple, symbolizing community commitment to the service of the Lord.

This word means 'stones' and refers to essential building materials. Stones are often symbolic of solidity and durability, representing here the foundations upon which the house of God will be built. Theologically, this evokes the idea that the Church, like the temple, is built on solid foundations, which are Christ and the faith of believers.

This term translates to 'craftsman' or 'woodworker', and it refers to those skilled in woodworking. It highlights the importance of skill and creativity in serving God. Spiritually, it reminds us that God uses the talents and gifts of each person for the building of His work.

This word means 'work' or 'task', and it implies an activity that requires effort and skill. In the context of the construction of the temple, it emphasizes that service to God is serious and sacred work. It teaches us that every act of service, whether great or small, has value in the kingdom of God.

15.epoque: This verse is set during the time of David, as he prepares for the construction of the temple in Jerusalem, a large-scale project for the people of Israel.
15.passage: In this chapter, David speaks to Solomon, his son, and conveys instructions regarding the construction of the temple, highlighting the necessary human and material resources to accomplish this divine work.
15.culture: In Israelite culture, manual labor and craftsmanship were highly valued, and artisans played a key role in society, particularly in the construction of places of worship.
15.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God equips His people with talents and resources to accomplish His will. The diversity of skills mentioned here underscores the importance of collaboration in serving God.
15.commentaire: This passage encourages us to recognize and value the gifts that God has placed in us and around us. Every believer has a role to play in the building of the Church, and we must be ready to engage in service, using our talents for His glory.

mots.sens: This term designates God in His creative and sovereign power. It is often used to express divine majesty and authority. In this verse, it reminds us that it is the Lord who gives strength and the ability to act, thus highlighting man's dependence on God to carry out his plans.

This word means strength or might. It evokes the ability to overcome obstacles and accomplish difficult tasks. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes that action must be undertaken with the strength that God provides, indicating that human effort must be accompanied by divine power.

This verb means 'to do' or 'to act'. It implies a concrete action, an implementation of plans. In this passage, it invites us to take action, emphasizing that faith must be translated into works, and that commitment is essential in the believer's life.

The name of the Lord, representing the covenant between God and His people. It symbolizes God's faithfulness and constant presence. In this verse, it reminds believers that their success depends on God's presence and assistance in their endeavors.

16.epoque: This passage is set in the time of David, when the king is preparing for the construction of the temple in Jerusalem, a project of great spiritual and national importance for Israel.
16.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David speaks to his son Solomon and gives him instructions for the construction of the temple. This verse highlights God's provision of resources and the encouragement to act with the certainty that the Lord will be present.
16.culture: In Israelite culture, the construction of the temple was an act of devotion and sacrifice, symbolizing God's presence among His people. The materials mentioned (gold, silver, bronze, iron) were symbols of wealth and prosperity.
16.interpretation: This verse teaches us that, although material resources may be abundant, the essential thing is to act with God's presence and help. It reminds us that our success in our endeavors depends on our relationship with the Lord.
16.commentaire: This passage encourages us to act with courage and determination, while recognizing that our strength comes from God. As believers, we are called to undertake concrete actions for the kingdom of God, relying on His power. Whether in our personal or community projects, we must always seek the direction and blessing of the Lord.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to help' or 'to assist'. It evokes the idea of providing active and tangible support, often in a context of need or weakness. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of solidarity and assistance among the members of God's people, highlighting the collective responsibility towards the leaders chosen by God.

This word means 'son' and can also refer to a descendant or a member of a lineage. In the context of the Bible, it is often used to establish familial and spiritual relationships. Here, it underscores the continuity of God's promise through David's lineage, reinforcing the idea that Solomon's leadership is an extension of God's plan for Israel.

This term means 'king' and designates the sovereign authority over a people. In Israel, the king was seen as God's representative on earth, tasked with governing according to divine laws. In this verse, it reminds the leaders of Israel of the importance of supporting King Solomon in his mission to build the temple, a sacred task that requires the unity and commitment of the entire nation.

17.epoque: This passage is set at the end of David's reign, around the 10th century BC, at a time when Israel was unified under one king and the construction of the temple in Jerusalem was about to begin.
17.passage: In this chapter, David prepares the transition of power to his son Solomon, encouraging him and mobilizing the leaders of Israel to assist him in the task of building the temple. This marks a key moment in Israel's history, where worship and the presence of God must be established permanently.
17.culture: In Israelite culture, unity and collaboration among leaders were essential for the success of common endeavors, particularly those related to faith and worship. Mutual support was seen as a moral and spiritual obligation.
17.interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of unity and community support in realizing divine projects. It reminds us that each member of the community has a role to play in fulfilling God's purposes, especially when it comes to promoting faith and honoring God through concrete actions.
17.commentaire: David, as king, recognizes the necessity of collective commitment to successfully carry out the construction of the temple, a symbol of God's presence among His people. This passage teaches us that in our Christian walk, we are called to support our leaders and work together for the advancement of God's kingdom. Every contribution, big or small, is valuable in the divine plan.

mots.sens: This term designates God in all His power and majesty. It is often used to express divine sovereignty over creation and humanity. In this verse, it reminds the Israelites that their God is present with them, ensuring their safety and success. The theological significance lies in recognizing God's active presence in the life of His people.

This word means 'rest' or 'peace'. It evokes the idea of tranquility of mind and physical security, resulting from divine protection. In this context, it emphasizes that God has granted His people a time of peace, allowing them to focus on their relationship with Him and their mission. It also reflects God's promise to give rest to those who trust Him.

This verb means 'to give' or 'to grant'. It implies a deliberate action on God's part, who offers blessings and resources to His people. In this verse, it is used to signify that God has given the Israelites victory over their enemies, illustrating His faithfulness to His promises. It underscores the notion that spiritual and material successes come from divine grace.

This verb means 'to serve' or 'to be subject to'. It evokes the relationship of dependence and allegiance between the people and God. In this context, it emphasizes that the land is subject to the Lord, which implies a recognition of His sovereignty. It reminds believers of their call to serve God and live under His authority.

18.epoque: This passage is set in the time of David, as he prepares for the construction of the temple in Jerusalem, marking a period of stability and prosperity for Israel.
18.passage: In 1 Chronicles 22, David speaks to his son Solomon and reminds him of God's faithfulness to Israel. This verse highlights the victory that God has given His people and the importance of remaining in His ways.
18.culture: At this time, the conquest and possession of land were signs of divine blessing. Peace and security were essential for the communal and spiritual life of the Israelites.
18.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God's presence is a determining factor in our rest and security. It encourages us to recognize that our victories and peace come from our relationship with Him, not from our own efforts.
18.commentaire: This passage exhorts us to trust in God, who is always with us and grants us rest. In our struggles and challenges, we must remember that God has the power to give us victory. As believers, we are called to live under His sovereignty, to serve diligently, and to rest in His grace.

mots.sens: This word means 'heart' and refers not only to the physical organ but also to the center of emotions, thoughts, and wills. In this context, it calls for a total involvement of the inner being in the pursuit of God. Spiritually, this emphasizes the importance of fully engaging in our relationship with the Lord, setting aside the distractions of the world.

Translated as 'soul', this term refers to life, the very essence of an individual. It evokes the idea of a living being in its entirety, encompassing emotions and will. In the context of this verse, it underscores the necessity of sincere devotion and a spiritual quest that encompasses our whole being, thereby reinforcing our commitment to God.

This verb means 'to build' and is often used in the context of constructing houses or temples. In this verse, it is related to the act of building a sanctuary for God, symbolizing an act of devotion and service. Theologically, this reminds us that our lives should be a space consecrated to God, where His presence can dwell.

This term designates a 'sanctuary' or 'holy place', a space dedicated to the worship of God. It represents the meeting between the divine and the human, a place where God's holiness is manifested. Spiritually, this reminds us that our lives should be a sanctuary for God, where we seek and serve Him.

19.epoque: This passage is set in the time of David, as he prepares for the construction of the temple of the Lord, a monumental project for the people of Israel.
19.passage: In this chapter, David gives instructions to his son Solomon regarding the construction of the temple, emphasizing the importance of dedicating oneself to God and seeking Him with all one's heart.
19.culture: At this time, the construction of temples was a central act in religious and social life, symbolizing God's presence among His people and their commitment to Him.
19.interpretation: This verse calls us to an active and passionate pursuit of God, fully engaging in our spiritual lives. It also reminds us that building a sanctuary for God is a collective work that requires everyone's participation.
19.commentaire: This passage exhorts us to invest our heart and soul in the quest for God, rising up to build a place of encounter with Him. As Christians, we are called to make our lives a sanctuary for the Lord, where His presence can manifest and where we can worship and serve with devotion.
